Quick update: I ran the crew pass and the Nano Banana Pro rules. Here's the prompt.

Աշխատում եմ **film-crew** (single-shot mode) → **banana-pro-director-2.0**-ով.

**Session start:** this folder isn't a git repo and has no NOTES.md, so I couldn't pull or check for open items. I changed no files, so there's no new NOTES entry.

**What I assumed** (the repo has no look or character references for this project, only a portfolio line: children's content, 2024, 60 pages):
- **Live-action photoreal look.** Most of the studio's work is live-action, and it's the skill's default. If the series is animated, tell me and I'll rewrite it as an illustrated key visual.
- **The two kids.** Their names come from verbs. Մտմտիկ (from «մտմտալ», "to ponder") is the dreamer who looks up and asks. Պրպտիկ (from «պրպտել», "to rummage") is the hands-on explorer who digs in and looks closer. I made Մտմտիկ a girl and Պրպտիկ a boy.
- **Title goes on later.** Nano Banana Pro often gets Armenian letters wrong, so the prompt keeps the top third as clean sky for the «Մտմտիկ և Պրպտիկ» logo, added in a design tool. The only "text" in the image is one big chalk question mark on a stone wall.

**Crew plan (one still, 4:5)**
- **Director:** the moment just before an answer. The same "why?" seen two ways: she looks up at the world, he looks down into it. Wonder, not mischief.
- **Production design:** an Armenian courtyard garden in late afternoon. A wall of warm pink tuff stone with the chalk "?", an apricot tree, dandelion seeds in the air, a garden snail on the stone. The props are a magnifying glass and a paper airplane.
- **Costume:** clear, readable shapes for small viewers. She wears a mustard-yellow cardigan over a striped tee, with two puffy pigtails. He wears a red (#D90429, the studio's one accent) hoodie with rolled sleeves, has a knee scuffed with soil and a messy cowlick.
- **Camera (DP):** low camera at the kids' eye height, 35mm-equivalent, a little low so they look heroic. Golden backlight from the upper right with soft fill from the front. A warm, fresh grade with clean sky in the top third for the title.

**Mode:** 3A (characters in a scene), Nano Banana Pro, 4:5, no references.

**Before you post it:** the faces are newly generated children, so check that they don't look like any real child. Use only Nano Banana Pro's 4:5 setting for the shape; the ratio is deliberately not in the prompt text. If you plan more posters or episodes with the same kids, pick the best result and use it as their face reference from then on (Mode 0/2).

## FINAL

**Mode 3A — key visual poster, Nano Banana Pro, 4:5**

**Settings:** Nano Banana Pro · aspect ratio **4:5** (set in the UI) · resolution 2K (4K for print) · no reference images · generate 4 and pick the best.

```
A warm cinematic still photograph captured on a real film set in late-afternoon golden light — a low-angle hero composition of two small curious children in a sunlit Armenian courtyard garden, the camera placed right at the children's eye height and tilted slightly upward so they feel big, brave and full of wonder, both children filling the lower half of the frame, a wide band of soft clean pale sky and glowing apricot leaves open across the upper third, the whole image holding a bright, gentle feeling of discovery just before an answer arrives.

On the left of the frame stands a thoughtful little girl with dark brown hair in two puffy pigtails, a few loose strands catching the backlight, rosy cheeks and big dark eyes. She wears a mustard-yellow knitted cardigan over a navy-and-white striped tee. She tilts her head back, one finger resting on her chin, gazing up in wonder at a white paper airplane drifting above her through the floating dandelion seeds, her mouth open in a small amazed "oh". On the right a lively little boy crouches low on one knee, a messy cowlick of chestnut hair sticking up, a little soil smudged on the knee of his jeans. He wears a bright red hoodie with the sleeves pushed up, and holds a big round magnifying glass up to his face, his one eye hugely enlarged behind the lens with delight as he peers at a garden snail climbing the stone beside him. The two children share the moment with joyful open faces, honest, natural and unposed.

Behind them rises an old wall of warm pink volcanic tuff stone, soft and weathered, with a large childlike question mark drawn in thick white chalk centered between the two children. Above the wall leans a leafy apricot tree with a few ripe orange apricots, and dandelion seeds float through the air, glowing as they cross the light. Grapevine leaves spill over the wall edge on the right, and terracotta pots with red geraniums sit at its base.

The low sun backlights both children from the upper right, wrapping their hair and shoulders in a soft golden rim, while gentle warm bounce from the sunny courtyard floor fills their faces evenly and kindly, with soft open shadows and bright catchlights in their eyes. The background falls into a gentle soft focus so the two children and the chalk question mark read clearly from far away.

Captured with a 35mm-equivalent lens at a moderately wide aperture on a real cinema camera — creamy natural bokeh in the leaves and floating seeds, soft frame-edge falloff, a light diffusion lifting the highlights into a gentle warm glow, a clean fresh color-negative daylight rendition with saturated but natural apricot, mustard, red and sky-blue tones, fine 35mm grain, in a joyful family-film narrative register. Real photographic frame captured on a real cinema camera, real children with natural soft skin, real knitted wool and cotton, real chalk on real tuff stone, real leaves and sunlight — no CGI, no rendered look, no digital cleanliness, no plastic surfaces, no AI smoothness, no skin smoothing, no glossy highlights, no extra text or letters anywhere in the image besides the single chalk question mark.
```
